records.why: On the 'No More Ransom' project (founded by Europol) saving ~200,000 computer users worldwide from paying $108M+ to ransomware criminals—a public-private anti-ransomware partnership (est. July 2016, at nomoreransom.org in 35 languages) offering free tools to decrypt files locked by famous ransomware, with 42 law-enforcement agencies and 100+ partners (F-Secure, Mastercard) (ransomware/anti-ransomware).

records.label: cyber
records.why: An F-Secure piece—an experiment using public WiFi to break into UK politicians' accounts showed a lack of basic security understanding—amid PM David Cameron's push (following FBI's Comey) to ban strong encryption 'so there's no safe space for terrorists', criticized by security pros as showing a fundamental misunderstanding of how security works (encryption debate/pentest).

records.label: cyber
records.why: A roundup of the 10 most powerful free hacking programs for Windows (defining hacking as unauthorized access)—for learning ethical hacking to protect devices—leading with Nmap (Network Mapper), the popular open-source port-scanner for network discovery and security auditing, amid SQL injection, XSS, WiFi/password cracking, and vulnerability scanning (hacking tools).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On the rise of phishing distributed from legitimate sites—attackers abusing companies' account-registration/newsletter/feedback forms (which need only a name and email) to have the legitimate site send a modified confirmation email containing an ad/phishing link, bypassing content filters and harming customer trust (per Kaspersky) (phishing technique).

records.label: cyber
records.why: A cybersecurity blog index—articles on AI's pros/cons in cybersecurity, threat vs vulnerability vs risk, why IAM is indispensable, remote-work security strategies, and cyber resilience (the ability to continue operations despite cyber incidents), citing Ponemon that 76% of US SMBs faced a cyberattack in 2019 (cybersecurity content).

records.label: cyber
records.why: A real-case study of a website that was hacked—how the owner discovered it (Google Analytics traffic dropped to zero, the site deindexed by Google), the disaster to its ranking after the intrusion (malicious code injected), and how SEO experts handled it; a website-hacking incident/recovery case study (website security).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On the evolution of Chinese cyber-espionage—from a decade ago's low-level phishing to steal IP from US firms, to today's more sophisticated 'decentralized' and 'ghostly' hard-to-attribute digital attacks (per the NYT and a Biden-administration indictment)—run by PLA units and a network of front companies/universities under China's MSS/MFA (state cyber-espionage).

records.label: borderline
records.why: An explainer on the deep web (only ~4% of web content publicly accessible/indexed, 96% deep) and the dark web—the deep web being private databases (emails, financial/medical records), and the dark web a small subset on darknets reachable only via specialized software (Tor)—and how they differ; a deep-web/dark-web explainer (borderline).

records.label: not_cyber
records.why: A review of McAfee True Key—McAfee's password manager (part of its antivirus suite)—covering strengths/weaknesses, features, pricing, MFA, and ease of use, concluding better standalone options exist; a security-software (password-manager) review, product review, not cybersecurity subject matter.

records.label: cyber
records.why: A Kaspersky piece on Windows 7 reaching end of support (Jan 14, 2020)—no more patches means new vulnerabilities will remain unfixed, and cybercriminals constantly seek flaws to plant malware to steal data/control systems—recalling how during WannaCry (2017) Microsoft exceptionally patched EOL XP/Server 2003, and advising upgrading to Windows 10 (patching/vulnerabilities).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On two serious security attacks—a Trojan (per Russian firm Doctor Web, dubbed 'Linux.BtcMine.174', a 1,000+-line 'programming cocoon') that's the first effective attack on Linux systems, harnessing the PC's power to mine cryptocurrency—and a phishing attack tricking bank customers into 'updating' their data on Google Maps to steal their banking details (malware/phishing).

records.label: not_cyber
records.why: A description of PrivateFirewall—a firewall tool for Windows PCs/servers with a desktop firewall, port manager, URL filtering, process monitoring, and behavioral anomaly detection against viruses/Trojans/spyware; a security-software piece, product marketing, not cybersecurity subject matter.

records.label: cyber
records.why: On the looming threat to encryption—the consensus that quantum computers will be able to break all current public-key encryption methods—explaining how public-key crypto (public/private key pairs generated from large prime factors) protects most sensitive data, that it's practically unbreakable today, and the need for leaders to act before attackers steal government/industrial secrets (cryptography/quantum threat).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On Symantec's ISTR (vol. 24) finding cybercriminals making millions from formjacking as ransomware/cryptojacking profits fall—drawing on 123M attack sensors (blocking 142M threats/day across 157 countries)—with Saudi Arabia's email malware rate four times the global average (1 in 118 emails vs 1 in 412) (threat report).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On the SolarWinds breach—US officials realizing in December 2020 that the hacking group 'APT29'/'Cozy Bear' (believed part of Russia's SVR) had breached many US agencies (Defense, Treasury, Commerce, State, DHS, NIH), reading emails at will—one of the most sophisticated and largest cyberattacks on federal systems ever, hitting Pentagon nuclear labs and Fortune-500 firms (state cyber-espionage/supply chain).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On Microsoft's online-security defense programs—helping form the Cybersecurity Tech Accord (a pledge to protect people from cyber threats), the FIDO Alliance (open authentication standards), MAPP (early vulnerability info for security vendors), MVI (antivirus integration with Windows), VIA (malware-info sharing), and FIRST (incident-response teams) (cybersecurity programs).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On the Arab Administrative Development Organization hosting an 'Arab Information Security' workshop—Lebanon's cybercrime-bureau head on fighting information crimes, an EC-Council-certified expert (Adel Abdel-Moneim) explaining anti-digital-forensics/evidence-invalidation techniques and social-media vulnerabilities, and lectures on IS security standards—with participants from Oman, Qatar, Saudi ministries (cybersecurity workshop).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On Microsoft Morocco and French cybersecurity firm Mailinblack extending their partnership to Africa—giving Moroccan SMEs advanced protection against email attacks (malware, phishing, ransomware, spam) by combining Office 365 security with Mailinblack's defense tech—since SMEs often lack basic protection against common threats (email security).

records.label: cyber
records.why: An explainer on what cybersecurity is (the first line of defense for computers/systems/data against malicious attacks) and famous cyberattacks—the 1988 Morris worm (exploiting a Unix flaw, self-replicating to cripple internet infrastructure; its author Robert Tappan Morris the first convicted under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, now an MIT professor) and the 2011 Canada government hack (cybersecurity/attacks).

records.label: not_cyber
records.why: An explainer on WooCommerce hosting (WordPress hosting optimized for WooCommerce—caching, custom DB tables, Elasticsearch, premium plugins); a web-hosting explainer, the 'WAF'/'malware'/'SSL certificates' keywords are a false positive (hosting-feature mentions).

records.label: cyber
records.why: A Google Help article on keeping your device safe—if you're redirected, see pop-ups/unwanted toolbars, or odd Google results, your PC may be infected with malware—listing symptoms and how to find/remove suspicious programs (browser hijackers like BrowserProtect, Omiga plus) or use antivirus (malware detection/removal).

records.label: not_cyber
records.why: A description of McAfee LiveSafe—a comprehensive cybersecurity solution (antivirus, firewall, network/web security, password manager, identity-theft protection, parental controls, secure storage, VPN) across Windows/Mac/Android/iOS; a security-suite product piece, product marketing, not cybersecurity subject matter.

records.label: cyber
records.why: On the Clubhouse audio-chat app confirming a user-data leak—a user found a way to stream some room audio to another site (despite the app's no-recording promise)—with researchers (Stanford Internet Observatory's David Thiel, and Robert Potter) stressing it was a data 'leak' (ToS violation), not a malicious 'breach', and Clubhouse banning the user and adding safeguards (data leak).

records.label: cyber
records.why: An interview with Oman's Public Prosecutor on IT-crimes—the accelerating rise of information-technology crimes and their varied forms, that the law criminalizes many acts against network/IT users (the most common being violating the integrity/confidentiality of data and information systems), with statistics (3,611 IT-crime cases in 5 years) and penalties for threats/extortion (cybercrime prosecution/law).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On Android 8.0 Oreo's new 'Install Unknown Apps' security feature—addressing Android's most-cited criticism (protecting users from malicious apps)—with Google Play Protect now built-in, and explaining how malware developers now upload a compliant app to the Play Store first, then use it to sideload the harmful component (Android app-security feature).
